title: Startup, shutdown & crashes
blurb: Won't turn on, slow to start, blue screens, restarts by itself, won't shut down.

remedies.title: Computer won't turn on
remedies.why: A flat battery, a faulty charger or socket, or the computer is on but the screen is off.

steps.text: Plug in the charger and leave it 15–30 minutes; look for a charging light. Try another socket.
Hold the power button 15–30 seconds, release, then press it normally.
Listen for fans and look for keyboard lights: if you see them, the computer is on and the screen is the problem (try an external monitor).
Unplug everything (docks, USB drives) and try again.
For a Mac with Apple silicon, try another USB-C charger and cable if you have one.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT the model and what you see (lights, fan sounds, beeps).

remedies.title: Computer takes ages to start up
remedies.why: Many apps start with the computer, updates finish at startup, or the disk is slow or full.

steps.text: Turn off startup apps you don't need (sort by Startup impact).
Turn off login items you don't need.
Free up disk space.
Let pending updates finish, then restart once more.
Run the Health check.

remedies.title: Blue screen ("Your PC ran into a problem")
symptoms: your pc ran into a problem
remedies.why: Windows stopped to protect itself, usually because of a driver, failing hardware (memory, disk) or damaged system files.

steps.text: Note the stop code shown (e.g. CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED); it points to the cause.
Undo what changed last: a new device, driver or update. Settings › Windows Update › Update history › Uninstall updates if it started after one.
Look at Reliability Monitor for the failing driver or app around the crash time.
Repair system files.
Test the memory (restarts the PC).
Check the disk's health.
If Windows won't start, it opens Automatic Repair after two failed starts: choose Advanced options › Startup Repair or System Restore.

remedies.escalate: Give IT the stop code, how often it happens and what changed before it started.

remedies.title: Computer restarts or shuts down by itself
symptoms: your computer restarted because of a problem
remedies.why: Scheduled updates, overheating, a power problem, or a crash that restarts automatically.

steps.text: Overnight restarts are often updates: set active hours so Windows doesn't restart while you work.
Look for crashes in Reliability Monitor ("Windows was not properly shut down").
"Your computer restarted because of a problem": after it starts, check for updates, remove recently added extensions or drivers, and unplug accessories.
Keep vents clear; a hot computer shuts down to protect itself.
Try another charger and wall socket.

remedies.title: Computer won't shut down or takes forever
remedies.why: An app won't close, updates are installing, or a device driver hangs.

steps.text: If it says updates are installing, wait; turning it off can damage Windows.
Save and quit apps yourself before shutting down; look for apps asking to save.
If stuck for over 30 minutes with no disk light, hold the power button 10 seconds.
Unplug docks and USB devices and try again.
Look in Reliability Monitor for apps that hang at shutdown.

remedies.title: Black screen after signing in (maybe with a cursor)
remedies.why: The desktop (Explorer) didn't start, the display is set to a screen that's not there, or a graphics driver failed.

steps.text: Press Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B to restart the graphics driver.
Press Windows+P twice and Enter to cycle display modes, in case it's showing on a missing screen.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Delete › Task Manager › Run new task › explorer.exe.
Restart the desktop: Explorer.
Unplug external monitors and restart.

remedies.title: Windows won't start (repair loop, "Preparing Automatic Repair")
remedies.why: Damaged startup files, a failed update, or a disk problem.

steps.text: Unplug USB drives and docks; a USB drive can be tried as the startup disk by mistake.
In the blue Recovery screen choose Troubleshoot › Advanced options › Startup Repair.
Then try Advanced options › Uninstall Updates › latest quality update.
Or System Restore to a point before the problem (your files stay).
If BitLocker asks for a recovery key, find it at aka.ms/myrecoverykey with your Microsoft or work account.

remedies.escalate: For "no bootable device" or disk errors, stop and tell IT: the disk may be failing.

remedies.title: Mac won't start (question mark, circle with a line, stuck on logo)
remedies.why: macOS can't find or load its startup disk, or an update didn't finish.

steps.text: Unplug everything except the charger and restart.
Start in safe mode: Apple silicon › hold power until options appear › select the disk › hold Shift › Continue in Safe Mode.
Open macOS Recovery (hold the power button until Options) › Disk Utility › First Aid on the startup disk.
From Recovery, Reinstall macOS keeps your files and apps.

remedies.escalate: If Disk Utility reports errors it can't fix, back up what you can and tell IT.

remedies.title: Problems that a shutdown doesn't fix (but a restart does)
remedies.why: With Fast startup on, Shut down saves part of Windows to disk, so problems survive it. Restart starts fresh.

steps.text: Use Restart when fixing problems.
Turn off Fast startup if you prefer: Power options › Choose what the power buttons do › Change settings that are currently unavailable › untick "Turn on fast startup".
